elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant retained as "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" — affiliate coverage is unconditional (no notice mechanic needed), though geographically confined to Authorized Locations, which is pre-existing scope language.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered grant names only Sparkling and its affiliated companies; there is no reference to contractors, service providers or other third parties acting on Sparkling's behalf.

Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual only "as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated"; that is a fee-contingent term, not a perpetual paid-up licence.
No "irrevocable" language appears anywhere in the rendered grant or Section 17(a); continuation remains conditional on payment and on non-termination under Section 17.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Termination grounds retained in Section 17 include insolvency in addition to uncured material default, so termination is not limited to uncured material breach, and no edit narrows those grounds.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Grant now reads "a non-exclusive licence, transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition"; coverage is narrower than all successors (e.g. a pure sale of substantially all assets is not expressly named) but a successor transfer right now exists.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply because the retained grant already extends to "affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" outright, i.e. affiliate coverage is achieved without any written-notice precondition — a better-than-fallback outcome, and no duplicate affiliate wording was added.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "non-transferable" deleted from the grant and replaced with "transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition"; the otherwise contradictory Section 3(c) prohibition is carved out by "or to a successor in a merger or acquisition", so no retained sentence bars the transfer.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: affiliate coverage already sits in the grant unconditionally, and the new grant language plus the matching Section 3(c) carve-out delivers an operative M&A successor transfer right with no contradictory retained prohibition.

Preferred level fails on four elements the drafter did not attempt: no contractor coverage, no paid-up perpetual licence, no "irrevocable" wording, and Section 17 termination grounds still include insolvency rather than uncured material breach only. To reach preferred, add "and contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf" to the grant, state that on payment of all applicable fees the licence is perpetual and irrevocable, and delete the non-breach termination grounds in Section 17.

Minimality holds: the only deletion is "non-transferable", which the chosen transferability element requires, and the only insertions are the successor transfer right and the conforming Section 3(c) exception. No affiliate wording was duplicated, no survival tail, expense or procedural extras were added, and the Authorized Locations scope, additional-fee mechanic and Section 17(a) perpetuity-while-paid language are untouched.

Watch-point for the drafter (not a failure on the language shown): the Section 3(c) carve-out sits at the end of a compound covenant ("not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work"), so it also excepts assignment of the Agreement to an M&A successor while Section 20(d) reportedly still requires Garman's written consent to assignment. Either narrow the carve-out to "or transfer of the Work to a successor in a merger or acquisition" to keep this squarely a LICENSE edit, or confirm the Section 20(d) consent requirement is addressed under ASSIGN so the two clauses do not read inconsistently.

Intent is preserved: the exception added to Section 3(c) runs in Customer's favour only (it is a Sparkling covenant), no new Vendor assignment exception is created, and pricing, location and termination mechanics survive unchanged with no dangling cross-references or undefined terms.
